chapter: Early New Orleans bands and records
title: Limits of early recording equipment
summary: Bass and bass drum could not be used on early records because they knocked the needle out of the wax.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: They didn't have the equipment to bring out that tone. No. No. When the boys made a record, the bass and the bass drum, you couldn't use them. Because if you happened to hit on the bass drum it knocked the needle right out of the wax. The same with the bass. If you pull it like that, slap it, it knocked the needle right out of the wax. So therefore we had to play just with wood blocks on the rim of the little drum. And that was a handicap because you were used to hearing rhythm.
But today no. Every instrument, in fact every instrument has its own mic. Drum, piano, bass, they all have their own mic.
